before.label: Historians’ responses to postmodernism
before.description: Brings together disputes about evidence, narrative, realism, and social explanation. after.scope_note: Defences, critiques, and revisions of historical knowledge conflict. A collection with White’s afterword cannot stand for unanimous rejection of him. Primary introductions distinguish skeptical interpretation, practical realism, disciplinary criticism and empirical reassessments. Exact source notes separate the editors’ descriptions of essays from reading the essays themselves.

strands.title: Facts and interpretive significance
strands.focus: Jenkins accepts an actual past while disputing that facts determine a single interpretation.

strands.focus: The coauthors link tentative knowledge, archival inquiry and democratic discussion; their social history of knowledge remains an argument.

strands.title: Historical practice and outside scrutiny
strands.focus: Evans values practical experience while accepting White’s objection to a disciplinary monopoly on understanding it.

truthdebate.people: Expanded eight people to 28 selections, adding twelve shared identities. The nine Beyond the Cultural Turn contributors now have named methodological contexts; philosophical resources Putnam, Rorty, Steiner, Bennett and Peirce are not called historians or members of a unified school. Partner and Marwick appear through Evans’s specifically attributed discussion; Hobsbawm and Swidler supply acknowledged reading/commentary.
truthdebate.works_and_arguments: Read Jenkins original introduction and selected truth/fact discussion with specified notes; Appleby/Hunt/Jacob complete introduction and practical-realism section plus pragmatist opening; Evans complete introduction and all 45 notes; Bonnell/Hunt complete preface and selected introduction, and White afterword 315–318. Later electronic editions and unread sections are explicit. Ginzburg’s existing 1993 primary statement retained; the 1992 witness text could not be read through the attempted sources.
truthdebate.internal_distinctions: Eight distinctions separate skeptical interpretation, practical realism, disciplinary scrutiny, evidence/representation, comparative culture/practice, narrative categories, gender/body/self and internally divided reassessment. Jenkins’s acceptance of an actual past and factual dates and Evans’s acceptance of White’s outside scrutiny prevent caricatures.
truthdebate.incoming_connections: Seven contributions document White’s conference/afterword participation, Foucault’s specifically mediated use in Jenkins, Jacob’s science questions, Feierman’s African research, Rose/Bynum’s gender/body history, Hobsbawm’s manuscript reading and Samuel’s differently received interventions. Prior practice and philosophy links strengthened with actual named receptions.
truthdebate.outgoing_connections: Cultural and social reassessments now cite primary editorial descriptions of specific projects; these descriptions are not independent readings of the essay bodies. Existing Ginzburg criticism of White retained with an access limit, while new White contribution makes disagreement reciprocal. Holocaust/Broszat, Chakrabarty and McNeill qualifications unchanged.
truthdebate.evidence_and_interpretation: Two new primary records and upgrades of two not-checked books distinguish exact read scopes, intermediaries, later editions, editorial summaries and primary chapter evidence. Stable IDs, roster selections, original prose, directions and classifications preserved. Structural checks do not certify philosophical claims or a final resolution of historical objectivity.
